_comment: Release dates verified against the npm registry (registry.npmjs.org time field). Support windows follow each project's published policy; Angular = 6 months active + 12 months LTS from the major's release date. Regenerate the 'current' fields when bumping: npm view <pkg> version

angular.name: Angular
angular.cadence: Two majors a year, roughly May and November.
angular.policy: 6 months active support, then 12 months long-term support. An Angular major is out of support 18 months after release.

releases.headline: Signal Forms, the Resource API and @angular/aria go stable. OnPush becomes the default change detection strategy. HttpClient uses fetch by default. New @Service() decorator.
Vitest becomes the default test runner via the stable @angular/build:unit-test builder; Karma is deprecated.
Signals stabilise (effect, linkedSignal, toSignal). Zoneless change detection reaches developer preview maturity. Vitest support lands experimentally.
standalone: true becomes the default — no more standalone flag on new components. linkedSignal and resource() arrive in preview.
Zoneless change detection in experimental preview. Built-in control flow and deferrable views go stable. Material 3 support.
The rebrand and angular.dev. Built-in control flow (@if/@for/@switch) and @defer arrive. esbuild/Vite application builder becomes the default.
Signals land in developer preview. takeUntilDestroyed and DestroyRef. Required inputs. Standalone ng new schematic.
Standalone APIs go stable. Functional router guards, directive composition API. Legacy compiler compatibility removed.
Standalone components in developer preview — the beginning of the end for NgModules. Typed reactive forms. inject() becomes broadly usable.

rxjs.name: RxJS
rxjs.cadence: Irregular. RxJS 7 has been the stable line since 2021.
rxjs.policy: No formal LTS window. RxJS 8 is on hold pending the TC39/WHATWG Observable standard, so 7.8 is the production answer.

releases.headline: On hold by design: the maintainers are waiting for Observable to be standardised on the web platform so RxJS 8 can align with it rather than diverge. Do not plan around a date.
The current stable line. 7.8.2 is the latest patch.
firstValueFrom/lastValueFrom replace the deprecated toPromise(). retry() takes a config object. Much smaller bundles and better TypeScript inference.
The pipeable-operator break: .pipe(map(x => x)) replaced patched prototype methods (obs.map(...)). Everything since is a refinement of this model.
The patched-prototype era you will still meet in old codebases: import 'rxjs/add/operator/map' and obs.map(...).

vitest.name: Vitest
vitest.policy: No formal LTS. The Angular CLI pins a compatible range through @angular/build.

releases.headline: Browser Mode leaves experimental; providers move to separate @vitest/browser-* packages. poolMatchGlobs/environmentMatchGlobs and deps.inline/deps.external removed in favour of projects and server.deps.*.
The workspace config is deprecated in 3.2 in favour of the projects option in the root config. Annotation API added.
Reporter and snapshot overhaul.
First stable major, Vite 5 alignment.

pnpm.name: pnpm
pnpm.cadence: Roughly a major a year, in the first half of the year.
pnpm.policy: No formal LTS. Pin it with the packageManager field in package.json.

releases.headline: The big config break: settings no longer read from the pnpm field in package.json or from non-auth .npmrc — they move to pnpm-workspace.yaml and ~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml. npm_config_* becomes pnpm_config_*. pnpm is pure ESM, the store is a single SQLite database, supply-chain defaults are on (minimumReleaseAge, blockExoticSubdeps), and Node 22+ is required. allowBuilds replaces the onlyBuiltDependencies family.

Dependency lifecycle scripts no longer run on install — a direct response to the Rspack supply-chain attack. Opt packages in with pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies. Peer-dependency hashes in the lockfile move from MD5 to SHA256.
Lockfile format v9.
Lockfile format v6.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.policy: Angular pins a supported TypeScript range per major — check the compatibility table before upgrading either one.
